column3: “Window-lattice” is rendered “lattice,” and “if I will live” as “whether I shall recover.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB reorders the sentence.
“What was the appearance of the man?” is rendered “What kind of man was he?”
“An owner of hair” is rendered “a hairy man,” and “loincloth of hide” as “leather girdle.”
NASB supplies “the king” as subject, and renders “the king has spoken” as “the king says.”
The Hebrew “he answered” is kept; some read “he went up.” NASB adds “again.”
“Sought favor to him” is rendered “begged him.”
NASB sets the question in dashes.
The Hebrew says “he died”; NASB names “Ahaziah,” and moves “because he had no son” earlier.
